model: Aurora UPC, Single Compressor Water-Source Heat Pump
applies_to: WaterFurnace single-compressor water-to-air heat pumps with the Aurora controls and the Aurora UPC protocol converter.
summary: BACnet objects of the Aurora Universal Protocol Converter (UPC) on a single-compressor water-source heat pump, software version 1.01. The UPC sits on the Aurora Base Controller (ABC) and exposes zone temperature, setpoints, occupancy, fan, compressor and dip-switch points over BACnet MS/TP. Points marked as needing the AXB board only report with that board and its sensors fitted.
notes: Object names are the sheet's reference names; its display names (several just 'Set point') are not the BACnet object names.
Many points are marked 'do not map' in the source and are listed only for completeness.
The same PDF also carries N2 and LonWorks lists; only the BACnet list is captured here.
Multistate value numbers jump from MSV 1 to MSV 7 in the source; MSV 2-6 are not listed.
Alarm code meanings come from the alarm table in the Aurora UPC Application and Troubleshooting Guide (AG1568EW).
Transport and network settings come from AG1568EW; the points list itself does not state them.

source.title: Aurora UPC Points List (BACnet Points for Single Compressor WSHP)

integration.summary: Set BV 54 to External, then command occupancy on MSV 1 and let the UPC hold its occupied, unoccupied and standby setpoints (AV 5-10). Read MSV 11 for the operating mode and MSV 8 for the lockout code. The BAS can also act as the thermostat with BV 44-48 (G, O, W, Y1, Y2).

minimum_points.name: schedule_selector_c
minimum_points.why: Must be External for BAS occupancy commands

minimum_points.name: alarm_reset_c
minimum_points.why: Reset manual-reset alarms (On, then back to Off)

minimum_points.name: compressor_status_st
minimum_points.why: Compressor output: off, low or high

integration.enable: The UPC runs its own internal weekday schedule until BV 54 schedule_selector_c is set to External (Active). Occupancy commands then go to MSV 1, or to AV 42 after BV 50 is set to AV. BV 25 e_stop_c shuts the unit down; BV 44-48 send G, O, W, Y1 and Y2 calls directly.
integration.remote_sensors: AV 4 zone_temp_ovrd_c replaces the zone sensor once BV 55 zone_temp_selector_c is set to BAS. AV 17 humidity_c, AV 22 co2_c and AV 24 voc_c take BAS values when no sensor is connected, and AV 26 oat_c takes an outdoor air temperature.
setup: Port 1a is the BAS port: EIA-485 for BACnet MS/TP (or N2), set by DIP switches, with baud 9600, 19.2k, 38.4k or 76.8k. It ships set to BACnet at 38,400 baud.
Port 1a can instead be jumpered for ARC156 (BACnet over ARCNET at 156 kbps). A LonWorks plug-in card uses port 1b and disables port 1a.
The MAC address is set on two rotary switches (tens and ones), 1 from the factory and 99 at most. The UPC only reads a new address after a power cycle.
The device instance is built from the network number and the MAC: network 7000 with MAC 12 gives 7012.
Wiring: 22 or 24 AWG shielded twisted pair, daisy-chained, polarity-sensitive (Net+, Net-, shield). About 30 devices and 2,000 ft per trunk; every MAC on a trunk must be unique.
gotchas: Dip switch overrides (BV 11-18) only reach the ABC while BV 22 is enabled. Record the physical switch settings first, and a slow-flashing yellow LED on the ABC means a switch is overridden.
Alarm reset: command BV 5 On, then back to Off. Loss-of-communication and over/under-voltage alarms reset themselves and cannot be reset from the network.
Zone sensor warm/cool adjust (AV 15, default 5 F) only shifts the setpoints in occupied or temporary occupied mode.
Points shown with * in the source need the AXB board and its sensors.
